title: Which solids share the same circle on the floor?
description: A cone stands on its base of radius four centimetres. The board finds its projection on the floor and then names other solids that give the same circle. Keeko's doubt is that different solids must give different projections.
teaching_notes: One idea: a projection shows the outline from above and cannot show height, so different solids can share one projection. Watch for students who expect one solid for each projection.

source: A cone standing on its base has base radius 4 cm. Name three
video_script.why: The child names solids with the same projection by asking what the circle on the floor shows, because the projection records the outline from above and not the height.
video_script.substitution: cone on its base, radius 4 cm; projection is a circle of radius 4 cm; an upright cylinder of radius 4 cm, a ball of radius 4 cm and a bowl with rim radius 4 cm give the same circle.
video_script.anchor: the cone standing on the floor with its circle drawn beneath it
video_script.wrong_answer: different solids must give different projections
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks each solid has its own projection, or we could not tell solids apart; but a taller cone has the same circle on the floor, because a projection from above does not show height, so the doubt is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: A cylinder, a ball and a bowl, each with radius four centimetres, give the same circle

final_answer.value: A cylinder, a ball and a bowl, each with radius 4 cm
final_answer.spoken: a cylinder, a ball and a bowl, each with radius four centimetres

hold_back: A cylinder, a ball and a bowl, each with radius 4 cm
maths_rules: the projection of an object is made by dropping every place of it straight down onto the plane, at a right angle
a given projection is not made by a unique object
the projection of a cone standing on its base is a circle of radius 4 cm
an upright cylinder of radius 4 cm, a ball of radius 4 cm and a bowl with rim radius 4 cm each give the same circle of radius 4 cm
wrong idea: different solids must give different projections; a taller cone keeps the same circle
video_script.design: One idea: the circle on the floor does not show height. The cone stands on the stage with its circle beneath; each new solid replaces it in turn and the circle stays in the same place.
